query: Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys reported to date commonly contain both solid solutions and intermetallic compounds. Induction-melted Al- and Mg-rich alloys reached densities of 2.64–2.75 g/cm3 but all had complex structures; Al20Be20Fe10Si15Ti35 combined a density of 3.91 g/cm3 with 911 HV hardness and oxidation resistance at 700 and 900 °C; compositionally graded MgAlCuZnGd showed region-dependent compression, plasticity, and corrosion behavior; and reported AlMgₓTiSnZn alloys contained a primary BCC constituent together with intermetallic compounds, with x = 1.0 showing the best property combination in that series. Prior studies have emphasized hardness and room-temperature compression, whereas interfacial segregation, interfacial energy, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance remain insufficiently studied. The design must retain a density below 6 g/cm3 and address performance constraints associated with the tendency of Mg and dissimilar constituent elements to form stable intermetallic compounds. Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state, what single intervention hypothesis could improve its combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance? State the intervention, its proposed causal mechanism, quantitative or directional predictions relative to the as-processed baseline, the composition and operating or test boundaries, the prior experimental evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a controlled experiment with explicit observations that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Microalloying with Ni can improve the combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance of a Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy.
generation.conditions: Low density (< 6 g/cm3), high strength, and high ductility
generation.mechanism: Ni microalloying increases the elastic modulus and reduces the atomic radius, leading to improved strength and ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and ductility, as well as enhanced corrosion resistance and high-temperature oxidation resistance
generation.boundary: Density < 6 g/cm3, temperature range for corrosion and oxidation testing
generation.uncertainty: Optimal Ni content and processing conditions for maximum performance improvement

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys with varying Ni contents, and test their mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation properties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with the optimal Ni content does not exhibit improved performance compared to the baseline alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

Enhancing the Strength and Ductility Synergy of Lightweight Ti-Rich Medium-Entropy Alloys through Ni Microalloying

Abstract: AbstractMedium-entropy alloys (MEAs) have attracted considerable attention in recent decades due to their exceptional material properties and design flexibility. In this study, lightweight and non-equiatomic MEAs with low density (~5 g/cm3), high strength (yield strength: 1200 MPa), and high ductility (plastic deformation: ≧10%) were explored. We fine-tuned a previously developed Ti-rich MEA by microalloying it with small amounts of Ni (reducing the atomic radius and increasing the elastic modulus) through solid solution strengthening to achieve a series of MEAs with enhanced mechanical properties. Among the prepared MEAs, Ti65Ni1 and Ti65Ni3 exhibited optimal properties in terms of the balance between strength and ductility. Furthermore, the Ti65Ni3 MEA was subjected to thermo-mechanical treatment (TMT) followed by cold rolling 70% (CR70) and cold rolling 85% (CR85). Effect of Mo on the Mechanical and Corrosion Behaviors in Non-Equal Molar AlCrFeMnNi BCC High-Entropy Alloys

Abstract: AbstractCo-free body-centered cubic (bcc) high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are prepared, and the elevated mechanical property and corrosion property of the Al0.4CrFe1.5MnNi0.5Mox (x = 0 and 0.1) alloys are studied. The Vickers hardness (HV) of the as-homogenized state is between HV 350 and HV 400. Both alloys are provided with nano-scale NiAl-rich B2 precipitates which contribute to the strength at high-temperature. In addition, adding Mo in the present alloy strengthens by σ phase. Al0.4CrFe1.5MnNi0.5Mo0.1 exhibited outstanding tensile properties, with a yield strength of 413 MPa and ultimate tensile strength of 430 MPa in the elevated tensile test at 600 °C, which is better than that of Al0.4CrFe1.5MnNi0.5 alloy.
